title: Keep specimen intake, specimen processing, derived task intake, and task execution separate
abstract: Specimen intake, the queue or work state for processing selected specimens, queues of downstream tasks generated by specimen analysis, and execution of those downstream tasks are four distinct stages. Entry into an upstream stage must not automatically enroll, authorize, begin, or complete a downstream stage. Each stage requires its own explicit selection and status record.

source.reference: Direct rule proposal; original conversation and private phrasing not retained

unresolved: Determine whether the phrase specimen-processing queue means an independently queued analysis stage, execution of the specimen queue, or both; preserve separate intake and processing states in either case.
Clarify that derived task queues are not automatically populated or executed merely because specimen analysis produced recommendations.
remarks: This is intake only. No specimen processing, catalog publication, downstream task creation, or task execution is authorized by the queue entry.
